extracted.intended_audience: employers, industrial managers, steelworks owners, and labor-relations practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and standards for employers on preventing, negotiating, and resolving labor disputes in industrial works (especially steelworks), including negotiation tactics, contractual arrangements, personnel policies, and welfare measures to maintain stable employer–worker relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never employ new men to replace strikers
rubrics_metrics.description: "My idea is that the Company should be known as determined to let the men at any works stop work; that it will confer freely with them and wait patiently until they decide to return to work, never thinking of trying new men—never."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and maintain a policy of allowing work to stop rather than substituting new labor; replacement hires are difficult to find for complex machinery and will alienate remaining workers. Anti-pattern: trying to run works with new men converts previously supportive old hands into lukewarm or hostile supporters of the strikers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not yield to extortionate demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Firm should not agree to unfair, coercive demands made under leverage (e.g., a demand for the whole sixty per cent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refuse unrealistic demands even under pressure from urgent contracts; yielding to an attempt to "take it by the throat and say, 'Stand and deliver'" is improper. Maintain principled negotiation rather than capitulation to force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let men settle disputes among themselves when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: A tactic is to tell the men: 'There is a labor dispute here and you must settle it between yourselves. The firm has made you a most liberal offer. The works will run when the dispute is adjusted, and not till then. Meanwhile your places remain open to you.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the responsibility on the workers to resolve internal disputes; this can avoid employer-imposed compromises and discourages disruptive strikes. Alternative: offer to run works only if the volunteer workforce accepts responsibility for their own protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish reputation for patient negotiation and non-aggression
rubrics_metrics.description: Be known to 'confer freely with them and wait patiently until they decide to return to work' and avoid aggressive tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reputation for fair, patient dealing reduces conflict. Combine openness to discussion with a firm refusal to use replacement labor. This balances courtesy with resolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sliding-scale wage arrangements tied to product prices
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a sliding scale based on the price of the product, with a minimum guaranteed wage and multi-year duration (example: a three-year scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sliding scales make capital and labor partners by sharing prosperity and adversity; include a minimum to ensure living wages. Prefer no fixed end-date, but allow six months' or a year's notice on either side. Avoid yearly scales that invite recurrent struggles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require individual worker signatures on long-term agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: When permitting union officers to sign, also require every workman to sign for himself because 'this scale lasts for three years ... if we have his signature also, there cannot be any misunderstanding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Securing individual signatures prevents disputes over union authority and can undercut union dues/payment (dissolving ineffective unions). Anti-pattern: relying solely on union officers' signatures for multi-year commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insist on honoring agreements; penalize breaking agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Breaking an agreement is dishonorable: 'The worst day that labor has ever seen ... is that day in which it dishonors itself by breaking its agreement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce agreements rather than reward breach. If men break an agreement, the employer is justified in refusing concessions and in making its own proposals (e.g., employer-submitted sliding scale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set voting rules for restarting works (use supermajority when strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works will not start until the men vote to do so by a two-thirds majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use voting thresholds as leverage to ensure broad consensus before resuming production; this prevents small factions from binding the workforce and provides negotiating time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet committees with courtesy and genuine interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive committees with 'great courtesy' and engage personally—Carnegie notes enjoying meeting workmen and praises courteous treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courtesy and personal engagement build trust. Address men respectfully (e.g., hat/off etiquette), listen, and treat them as 'gentlemen' to foster cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use situational social tactics to defuse or expose leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include socializing a delegation (showing them New York) to avoid immediate negotiation, or publicly rebuking a bully for discourtesy (ordering him to remove his hat) to neutralize his influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactical delay, social engagement, and moral rebuke can break leaders' control, reveal divisions, and produce voluntary, peaceful settlements. Anti-pattern: direct public confrontation that escalates violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and neutralize hidden instigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that disputes may be driven by a few instigators (e.g., a saloon-owner employed in the mills) whose influence can be curbed by exposing their motives or removing their standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate the roots of agitation and use moral pressure, arbitration, or internal discipline to isolate instigators rather than punishing general workforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide non-wage benefits to reduce grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: Concessions such as paying wages every two weeks instead of monthly, establishing a cooperative store, selling coal at net cost with delivery, and offering company-facilitated savings and home-loan trusts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-cost employer measures (more frequent pay, co-op stores, cheaper fuel delivery, savings plans paying interest, trust funds for loans) materially improve workers' welfare and reduce causes of complaint; they often yield high returns in loyalty and stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer company-supported savings/trust accounts and home loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer to take actual savings of each workman (up to $2,000) and pay six percent interest; keep money separate in a trust fund and lend for home-building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fosters thrift, security, and loyalty. Ensure funds are kept distinct from company capital and administered transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical amenities to assist prudent workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: cooperative purchasing to save costs for families; arranging delivery of coal at net cost to homes; paying wages more frequently to avoid shopkeeper indebtedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address logistical and economic pain points (monthly pay leading to debt) with pragmatic measures that cost little relative to the benefits in worker contentment and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fixed short-term scales that provoke recurring disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Yearly scales prompt constant preparation for struggle; better to set no fixed end-date, subject to reasonable notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer or open-ended arrangements (with notice periods) reduce frequency of renegotiation and associated conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize ignorance, not hostility, as root cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie: 'the main root of trouble is ignorance, not hostility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on education, explanation, and persuasion in discussions with workers. Employ patient reasoning rather than assuming ill will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat good employees as partners and value non-wage motivations
rubrics_metrics.description: Many disputes are not chiefly about dollars but appreciation, kind treatment, and fair dealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate gratitude and respect; small humane acts can be as effective as wage increases in securing loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to use lawful protection if needed, but weigh consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The superintendent and state officials used the sheriff and guards to protect replacement efforts; this had consequences given violent leaders with arms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use police or military protection only with full awareness of escalation risks and public perception; protective measures can entrench hostility if not carefully managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When employees sign agreements carelessly, enforce the agreement and insist on future caution
rubrics_metrics.description: If a worker signed without understanding a paper, the employer's stance was: carry out the provisions of the agreement one signs carelessly and resolve to be more careful next time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer enforcing written commitments to preserve contractual integrity. Simultaneously promote worker education to prevent future inadvertent signings.
